newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto chairman compensation up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto chairman compensation up in 1996.

text.p: Monsanto Co Chairman Robert Shapiro's total compensation rose 52 percent last year to $2,920,000 from $1,921,017 earned in 1995, according to a proxy statement.
Shapiro, who took over as chairman in April 1995, earned a 1996 base salary of $800,000 and a bonus of $2,120,000. His 1995 compensation consisted of base pay of $685,417 and a bonus of $1,235,600.
He served president and chief operating officer before he was appointed chairman.
Shapiro's base salary is now frozen at $800,000 under a compensation plan that ties bonuses to certain corporate goals.

The 1996 incentive award of $2,120,000 was granted in recognition of the company reaching its goals for net income and return on equity, and in recognition of sustained performance over the past three years, a spokeswoman said.
In addition, Shapiro received 2,950,000 premium priced options in 1996, which only can be exercised if the stock reaches certain target prices.
Those options include 590,000 exercisable at $30.338 a share, 885,000 exercisable at $35.00 a share, 885,000 at $40 a share, and 590,000 at $45.00 a share.
None of the options can be exercised before April 1997.
Shares in Monsanto were down 3/8 at 39-3/4 late Thursday afternoon.
